idea: Themed weeks, week five, School and health day: written from the source, then corrected by a numbers editor and a viewer editor before voicing.
description: In Uttar Pradesh, 69.9% of children aged 12 to 23 months were fully vaccinated in NFHS-5 (2019-21) and 81.4% in NFHS-6 (2023-24), a rise of 11.5 points. Vaccination is counted by vaccination card or mother's recall.

India's rate went from 76.6% to 82.6%, a rise of 6.0 points, so Uttar Pradesh's rise was 1.9 times India's. Uttar Pradesh's gap to India's rate was 6.7 points in 2019-21 and 1.2 points in 2023-24. The NFHS-6 fact sheets also print a card-only figure (India 87.1%), which is a different measure from the one used here, and the NFHS-5 figures are those printed in the NFHS-6 sheets. These are survey estimates, and small gaps are not differences. The map covers the 33 states and UTs with a figure in both surveys and leaves out Manipur (no figure), Chandigarh and Lakshadweep (small sample). The table shows how much, not why.
source: International Institute for Population Sciences, National Family Health Survey: NFHS-6 (2023-24) state fact sheets, which also print the NFHS-5 (2019-21) figure. Children aged 12 to 23 months fully vaccinated, by vaccination card or mother's recall (the sheets also print a card-only figure: India 87.1%). 33 states and UTs with a figure in both surveys; Manipur, Chandigarh and Lakshadweep have none. Survey estimates.

Numbers editor changed 'children' to 'one-year-olds' (12 to 23 months only), 'nearly twice' to '1.9 times', and the spoken gap, which did not match the spoken rates (now 6.7 points, then 1.2). Viewer editor replaced a hook that copied tn20's shape with one about the gap to India (6.7 points, then 1.2).
